title: Sausage pasta with watercress and lemon

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Sausages, dried pasta, crème fraîche, Parmesan and fresh watercress are all ordinary home ingredients with no jars or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Every item is a standard, everyday-priced line in any Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large pan, a frying pan and a grater, and the techniques are simple boiling and frying.

works.reason: 400g pasta, six sausages and 200ml crème fraîche loosened with pasta water make a sensible sauced pasta for four, and the timings line up.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers skinning the sausages, slicing garlic, zesting and grating, and the 12 minutes matches the pasta boil, so it fits a quick dinner.

honest_ingredients.reason: Penne is dried pasta, and every listed ingredient and seasoning, including pepper under 'season', is used with nothing unlisted.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm sausage pasta suits early March, and a full 100g of watercress is wilted through as a main component, named in the title, rather than scattered as a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family pasta with sausage protein and a good handful of peppery greens, the sort of thing people cook again.
